text.p: A secretary who never earned more than $15,000 a year but invested in the stock market left $18 million to a children's hospital where she often passed out teddy bears, a hospital spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Gladys Holm, who died last year at 86, sometimes spoke of "having something" for the Children's Memorial Hospital in her will, but no one dreamed it would amount to $18 million, Julie Pech said.
Holm retired in 1969 after 41 years as a secretary at American Hospital Supply Co. Her boss and the firm's founder, Foster McGaw, told her to invest any excess earnings in stocks and she obliged.
"When he would buy 1,000 shares, she would buy 10," Pech said.

Known as "The Teddy Bear Lady" by children and staff at the self-supporting hospital, Holm never married and had no heirs. She visited frequently and passed out hundreds of teddy bears after accompanying a friend's daughter to the hospital for treatment of a heart defect in 1952.
That little girl, now a 46-year-old history professor, remembered Holm as a vivacious, independent-minded woman who loved to tell stories while nursing a scotch at the dinner table.
"She was a very funny and feisty person who did what she wanted to do," said Lynne Adrian, 46, by telephone from her home in Tuscaloosa, Alabama.
Adrian said for many years, Holm was like a member of her family and gave presents to all the children. "She gave nice toys and stuff but we had no idea she was wealthy."
For many years, Holm cared for her ailing father, Adrian said, which along with her demanding job may have kept her from marrying.
Holm, who lived in a modest two-bedroom townhouse in a Chicago suburb, asked that her bequest fund research into pediatric illnesses.
